---
title: "crossmap explorer"
---

## What this is

A demo of the exploratory power of **crossmaps**
([xmap](https://github.com/cynthiahqy/xmap) R package;
[Huang 2024, arXiv:2406.14163](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2406.14163)),
using INDSTAT Rev.3's `isiccomb` combination-code splitting as a running
case study. See `CLAUDE.md` for the full architecture writeup.

- [Coverage](01-coverage-tiles.qmd) -- which country-years rely on a
  split at all, and how much
- [Explorer](02-crossmap-explorer.qmd) -- zoom into one country-year's
  `isiccomb -> isic -> isic.3` crossmap as a node-link diagram

## Component (d): whole-classification overview -- blocked

This page is meant to hold the **composed, whole-classification**
`isiccomb -> isic.3` view: one graph (not per country-year) showing every
place in the classification where a real one-to-many split or many-to-one
aggregation happens, with the pass-through-unchanged majority collapsed
out of view.

This is intentionally not built yet. It depends on
[`xmap::compose_xmap()`](https://github.com/cynthiahqy/xmap/issues/29)
(open, in progress) -- which chains `isiccomb -> isic` and `isic -> isic.3`
into a single composed crossmap via matrix-multiplication-style weight
composition, rather than materialising the intermediate `isic`-level
values at all. That composed crossmap *is* the input this page needs;
building a hand-rolled substitute here would just be reimplementing that
function early and would need throwing away once it ships.

**When `compose_xmap()` lands**: add a target to `_targets.R`

```r
tar_target(
  composed_isiccomb_isic3,
  compose_xmap(links_isiccomb_isic, links_isic_isic3)
)
```

and build this page against `composed_isiccomb_isic3` directly -- at that
point the "bundle one-to-one edges, show only many-to-one components"
reduction becomes a filter on the composed crossmap's weights/degrees,
not a graph algorithm to design from scratch.
